facts.label: Spinning disk seek
facts.note: Mechanical, so this one has not improved and will not.

facts.label: Round trip within one datacenter
facts.note: Bounded by switching and software, not distance.

facts.label: Round trip across continents
facts.note: Bounded by the speed of light in fibre, so no amount of engineering removes it. This is why replica placement is a product decision.

facts.label: Downtime per year at 99.999%
facts.note: 5.26 minutes. Below any human reaction time, so it implies automated recovery with no manual step.

facts.label: Round trip from a user to the nearest ISP node
facts.note: FCC Measuring Broadband America, via HPBN: fiber 10–20 ms, cable 15–40 ms, DSL 30–65 ms. 20 ms is a good wired broadband connection; mobile is usually worse. It is paid before a packet even leaves the user's city.

facts.label: Idle time before Linux TCP starts keepalive probes
facts.note: tcp_keepalive_time defaults to 7200 seconds, and keepalives are only sent on sockets that enable SO_KEEPALIVE. After that, 9 probes 75 seconds apart before the connection is declared dead. A phone that loses signal without closing its socket can look connected for hours as far as TCP is concerned.
